title: The motor cruise ship
standfirst: Most Nile cruises are on motor ships, from simple boats to the most expensive on the river. Here is what they are like and how they differ. This is one of the vessel types in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: What a Nile cruise ship is
paragraphs: A Nile cruise ship is a long, flat river ship of three to five decks: cabins on the lower decks, a restaurant and lounge, and a sun deck on top, usually with a pool. They are built narrow and low to pass the lock at Esna and the bridges on the way.

sections.heading: Life on board
paragraphs: Ships carry many more guests than a dahabiya, so there are more facilities: a pool, a bar, sometimes a spa or gym, and evening entertainment. Meals are often buffets. The sightseeing programme is set, and guides take groups ashore at each stop.

sections.heading: Schedules and moorings
paragraphs: Ships keep fixed timetables, typically four nights upstream from Luxor to Aswan and three nights downstream back to Luxor. At Luxor, Edfu and Aswan they moor at town quays, often several ships side by side, so guests may cross other ships’ lobbies to reach the shore and some cabins look onto the next ship.

sections.heading: Is a cruise ship for you?
paragraphs: Choose a ship for facilities, a fixed programme and a wide range of prices. Look at the deck and the cabin before you book: the same ship can have very different cabins, and the upper decks are usually quieter and brighter.

faqs.q: How many guests does a Nile cruise ship take?
faqs.a: Most carry between about eighty and a hundred and forty guests. Each ship’s page shows its own figure.

faqs.q: Do all ships have a pool?
faqs.a: Most do, on the sun deck. Each ship’s page lists its facilities.
